items.title: EU vies to expand role in Ukraine-Russia peace talks to influence US thinking
items.why: Shows how Brussels is trying to stop a US–Russia deal being made over its head, with the Abu Dhabi timing and Moscow's conditions.

items.title: Von der Leyen: a magyar változásokkal Európa is erősebb lett
items.why: Shows how the EU is rewarding [[p:Péter Magyar]]'s reforms with funds, in the same week Budapest held back Ukraine's next clusters.

items.title: With Kyiv's air defense crews as they race to keep up with Russia's jet-powered drones
items.why: Ground-level reporting on why fast jet Shaheds beat Kyiv's layered air defence, and what interceptors are coming.

items.title: Can the US still deter Russia? Lithuania navigates an uneasy alliance
items.why: On-record views from Vilnius on hedging against Washington while seeking permanent US troops; analysis.

items.title: New electronics reach Iran, but prices soar as gov't fees, US sanctions hit
items.why: A reporter in Tehran shows how the blockade and the UAE trade halt reach shop counters: smuggling through Sulaimaniyah, import duties of up to 30%, and a minimum wage of about $83 a month with the rial near 2.64 million per dollar.

items.title: הפעם אנחנו יודעים (This time we know)
items.why: Israel's senior columnist, writing on election eve, sets out what each outcome would mean for war, the judiciary and Arab citizens. He reveals that army chiefs Halevi and Zamir demanded Netanyahu's orders in writing, and argues the opposition should merge after the vote. This is opinion.

items.title: Itamaraty convoca representante da Argentina para explicar passagem de Flávio Bolsonaro pelo país
items.why: Follows the defeated candidate's exit minute by minute from Argentine migration records (bridge crossing, private jet, a flight plan to Guayaquil that ended in Miami), and explains why the summons is a pointed signal while the two countries have had no ambassadors since August.

items.title: Delcy Rodríguez volvió a prometer elecciones en Venezuela, pero no puso fecha y pidió "apoyar las reformas"
items.why: Sets out the interim government's sequence (amnesty, justice reform with EU help, a softer hate-speech law, talks with the 2015 National Assembly) that Caracas says must come before any vote, which matters now that Washington is talking about a 2027 timetable.

items.title: 'The alternative to diplomacy is war': Polisario warns of risks after collapse of Western Sahara UN mission
items.why: The Polisario's own reading of the MINURSO collapse, with Crisis Group on the risk of Algeria being drawn in.

items.title: Deadly RSF drone attacks reveal deep divisions between Sudan and Ethiopia
items.why: Lays out Khartoum's drone data and Addis Ababa's counter-charges behind the consulate expulsions. Most figures are Sudanese government claims.

items.title: The real reason IGP Dan Bahadur Karki was sacked
items.why: Insider-sourced account of how a police-chief dismissal and newsroom raids opened the first public rift in Balen Shah's government. Reasons come from unnamed officials.

items.title: 2026 enlargement report: what it says about Georgia
items.why: Clear chapter-by-chapter walk through the Commission's verdict on Georgia, including its four priority judicial reforms.
